prusament-pla-tds.title: Prusament PLA technical data sheet
prusament-pla-tds.scope: Archive member Prusament PLA/1_PLA_Prusament_TDS_2022_EN.pdf; Manufacturer measurements on FFF coupons for this commercial product; color, lot and reinforcement content are not specified. No raw replicate data or definition of the reported plus/minus term is supplied. Printed-coupon tensile results do not report conditioning, test temperature, test rate, detailed dimensions or specimen count. The 24 °C / 22% humidity footnote belongs to the separate moisture-uptake rows and is not treated as a tensile conditioning protocol.

astm-d638.title: ASTM D638-22 — Standard Test Method for Tensile Properties of Plastics
astm-d638.scope: Public scope and significance/use statements, not a reproduction of the full standard. This source does not establish that a supplier used D638 or complied with any particular procedure.

amza-2021.title: Accelerated Aging Effect on Mechanical Properties of Common 3D-Printing Polymers
amza-2021.scope: FFF specimens: opaque blue Fillamentum PLA Extrafill and transparent natural PrimaSelect PETG; Creality Ender-3, Cura 4.5, 100% grid ±45° infill, 0.2 mm layers, two contours. PLA nozzle/bed: 205/45 °C; PETG: 235/65 °C. Unaged controls are discussed separately from UV-B-aged groups; ASTM D638-14 Type I dimensions, 1 mm/min, 23 °C / 50% RH, five specimens per tensile group. Ultimate strength is distinct from the supplier yield property.

fischbach-2023.title: Effect of physical aging on the flexural creep in 3D printed thermoplastic
fischbach-2023.scope: Author manuscript, printed BASF Ultrafuse PLA; 100% infill, 0.2 mm layers, 215 °C nozzle, 30 °C bed; ISO 899-2 bending creep. The long-duration test uses one specimen under a 10 N nominal force for 170 h near 20 °C. No family-wide lifetime or reduction factor is inferred. The long-duration specimen had an initial age of five hours; the authors report laboratory relative humidity of 30–50%.

astm-d256.title: ASTM D256-26 — Standard Test Methods for Determining the Izod Pendulum Impact Resistance of Plastics
astm-d256.scope: Public scope and significance/use statements explain impact-test dependencies. No paid standard text or material-specific impact design value is reproduced.

stratasys-tooling.title: Design Considerations: FDM Additive Manufacturing Tooling
stratasys-tooling.scope: Industrial Stratasys FDM tooling guidance. It supplies design context, not qualification of the Prusament grades or a desktop printer. A precise publication date is not stated in the document metadata used here.

tensile-test-scope.locator: Public Significance and Use §§4.1, 4.3–4.5 and Note 5; Scope §1.1 and Note 1.
tensile-test-scope.finding: Tensile properties depend on specimen preparation, rate and environment; modulus characterizes the initial response. Testing over different load durations and environments is needed for engineering use. ASTM D638 and ISO 527-1 have differing technical content.

stiffness-vs-strength.locator: §2 and Table 1 (materials and printing); §3.2, Table 2, PLA Control and PETG Control columns.
stiffness-vs-strength.finding: In the unaged control groups, the tested PLA specimens had a higher modulus while the tested PETG specimens had a higher ultimate tensile strength. This is an independent printed-grade result, not a yield-stress comparison or a statement about all PLA and PETG.

direction-and-load-path.finding: The guide connects FDM orientation to directional strength and recommends a short, direct load path. Its process-specific statements are not universal Z-strength data.

prusa-orientation.locator: Archive member Prusament PLA/1_PLA_Prusament_TDS_2022_EN.pdf, PDF p. 3, orientation sketch; corresponding PDF p. 3 sketches in PETG, ASA and PC Blend sheets.
prusa-orientation.finding: The inspected source sketches show both tensile coupons with the long axis along X: Horizontal is flat XY, and Vertical xz is on-edge XZ. Those are not in-plane versus build-Z tensile tests. The corresponding series retain their own source locators.

creep-below-tg.finding: One printed Ultrafuse PLA specimen continued to creep under the long room-temperature bending hold below its glass transition. This evidence calls for a sustained-load check but does not supply a general lifetime prediction.

impact-test-scope.locator: Public Scope §1.1 and Notes 3–4; Significance and Use §§5.2, 5.7–5.9.
impact-test-scope.finding: Specimen preparation, notch, conditioning and failure type affect impact results. A no-break observation is not an unlimited impact resistance. Results from different impact methods and specimen configurations do not establish a common ranking.

industrial-tooling-context.locator: §1.4, printed p. 4, Volvo Trucks application context.
industrial-tooling-context.finding: The manufacturer documents industrial FDM use by Volvo Trucks for lifting devices and ancillary tooling. This passage does not identify the exact grade or load rating for each component.
